videos.headline: Cummins to Ollie Pope, out Bowled!! It's getting messy out there for England. Sure Pope has made a mess of his poles. Walked right across this length delivery looking to glance behind square, misses, the ball hits the back leg and smashed middle and leg. The ignition of the sticks under lights looks good. Surely for Australia! England have lost 7 wickets for 39 runs now. 48 more minutes for stumps. 3 wickets to go! Ollie Pope b Cummins 5(26)

Boland to Billings, out Caught by Cummins!! Nooo. Not any more of these soft dismissals please, England! Billings checks his flick shot and hits it straight to mid-on. Simple length delivery, but it jumped a bit more than Billings thought, which is why he thought, oh oh, do I need to adjust the bat speed? And in the process ended up offering a dolly. The replay suggest it was more a case of ball not coming onto the bat. Four more wickets for Australia, 54 minutes left in the day. Billings c Cummins b Boland 1(9)

Boland to Root, out Bowled!! Oh through him. Keeps low and the ball escapes under the bat to hit off stump. Root stands and smiles in disbelief. He did no wrong there. Was back of a length so he was on the back foot looking to defend, hears the timbaah. End of Root's Ashes, would have wanted a better second half for sure. Will Australia look to wrap this up today? Still an hour and 10 odd minutes to go. Root b Boland 11(31) [4s-1]

Starc to Stokes, out Caught by Lyon!! Bad shot from such an experienced batter and Starc roars with a double fist-pump. Short on the stumps, Stokes decides to take the pull on, but splices it in the air, there are two men in the deep on the on-side, deep square who is Lyon runs forward and dives to take a fine catch. Never looked like dropping that. Such good hands. But why would you play that when your side is 92/3 and in trouble. A poor tour for Stokes has ended with a horrible dismissal. Australia on top now. Stokes wanted to pull it down and is disappointed as he walks off. Stokes c Lyon b Starc 5(15)

Green to Crawley, out Caught by Carey!! Green has another. Ends Crawley's stay. Full and angled in on the fourth-stump channel, Crawley drives but the bat comes down at an angle, towards mid-wicket, thick outside-edge is neatly caught by Carey. Again Crawley fails to make use of a good start. Australia right back and now have the edge in the game. Crawley c Carey b Green 36(66) [4s-7]

Green to Malan, out Bowled!! 138.2kph , Green ends Malan's misery. The inipper from a good length, Malan defends away from the body with an angled bat and drags it back on. It was just a matter of time before Green got Malan, he was all over him and the no.3 was softened up with a blow to the helmet. Was never comfortable against the allrounder's round the wicket angle and perishes. End of Malan's Ashes tour. Green has brought Australia back into the contest. Malan b Green 10(20) [4s-2]

Green to Rory Burns, out Bowled!! Green with the golden arm. Rory Burns will be heartbroken to see this replay. He only tried to leave this short of length delivery ball, but it hit the bat and disturbed the sticks. Couldn't handle the bounce as he was a tad late to get the bat high. Sometimes this game is cruel. He didn't deserve to get out this way, but he looked so good out there after all those opening woes. Australia have something to cheer and will go back a bit more confident into the tea break. Rory Burns b Green 26(46) [4s-4]

Broad to Carey, out Caught by Billings!! Inside-edges one, again, and nobody has overstepped this time. A proper innocuous delivery this, full, way outside off, and Carey reaches out to try and drive. But the ball doesn't quite come on, nipping back in a touch as well to take the tentative under-edge to the keeper. Carey c Billings b Broad 49(88) [4s-4]

Broad to Green, out Lbw!! Looked pretty plumb and it was a surprise that Paul Wilson shook his head. Close to the crease and pitches on off, Green plays down the wrong line as he gets forward to defend, the ball holds its line to beat the outside edge and hit him on the pad in front of off, was crashing into the stumps. After it was given not out, the fielder shied at the stumps, hoping to catch Green short, but the ball ran away to the boundary as overthrows, till Root went for the review and was proved right. Green lbw b Broad 23(47) [4s-3]

Broad to Green, out Lbw!! Looked pretty plumb and it was a surprise that Paul Wilson shook his head. Close to the crease and pitches on off, Green plays down the wrong line as he gets forward to defend, the ball holds its line to beat the outside edge and hit him on the pad in front of off, was crashing into the stumps. After it was given not out, the fielder shied at the stumps, hoping to catch Green short, but the ball ran away to the boundary as overthrows, till Root went for the review and was proved right. Green lbw b Broad 23(47) [4s-3]

Mark Wood to Smith, out Caught by Woakes!! ** Fire, lots of fire ** Bodyline after bodyline after bodyline, Wood keeps giving it his everything, and he's managed to suck in the biggest fish in the Australian seas. It's a pretty straightforward bouncer, which Smith hoks, getting the top-edge for a simple reverse-cupping catch at fine leg. Smith c Malan b Mark Wood 27(62) [4s-4]

Mark Wood to Head, out Caught by Billings!! The short theory works. Head just didn't look comfortable in this short stay, and he ends up hopping to this leg-lined back of a length delivery, trying to glance it away, only to get a tickle off the glove through to the keeper. Head c Billings b Mark Wood 8(16) [4s-1]

Mark Wood to Boland, out Caught by Billings!! 144kph, the hard back of a length, seaming in, kicking up off the deck and cramping Boland up as he goes onto his back foot with a very tentative poke to end up nicking it off to the keeper. Wood's been bowling his heart out all series, and he's made sure the nightwatchman doesn't wag on. Boland c Billings b Mark Wood 8(33)

Woakes to Labuschagne, out Caught by Billings!! Another one down the leg-side. So many in this game. Short of a length angling down, Labuschagne glances and it's a healthy edge, Billings dives to his left to take his first catch in Tests. Labuschagne shakes his head as he walks back. England fighting back with wickets. Labuschagne c Billings b Woakes 5(11)

Broad to Warner, out Caught by Ollie Pope!! Warner out for a pair! He walks off with a wry smile on his face. Good catch from Pope at backward point. Broad gets Warner again. Short of a length outside off, Warner cuts in the air and Pope moves smartly to his right to take a sharp catch. That's the start England wanted. Warner c Ollie Pope b Broad 0(3)

Green to Billings, out Caught by Boland!! Billings has picked out long-leg to the short ball. He was looking solid on debut but has thrown it away. Short down leg, Billings pulls but top-edges it fine, Boland came in initially but then went back and took a smart catch. Not easy to pick the pink-ball under lights but the big man snaffled it well. Green with a double fist-pump and a roar. Deserved wicket for Green. Billings c Boland b Green 29(48) [4s-6]

Boland to Ollie Pope, out Caught by Carey!! He's been set up with three wide deliveries, a fourth full incoming ball on the stumps, and a fifth wide one floated outside off and sucking him in. Pope seriously didn't need to play at this, but he gets a stride in front, pushes away from his body and feathers it through to the keeper. Ollie Pope c Carey b Boland 14(23) [4s-3]

Starc to Stokes, out Caught by Lyon!! Oh wait! Isn't this into the ground? Nooo. Stunner from Lyon at backward point. Oh cricket gods, this shot deserved four runs. Stokes stood tall and absolutely muscled that back foot punch. Looked so good real time and even the cameraman was stunned a bit as he had to adjust and focus on Lyon. Looked like a boundary written on it, suddenly you saw Lyon diving low to take a brilliant catch. Even Starc couldn't believe. Big smile on his face. Stokes wanted to bat positively, didn't place this right and now England have slipped from 78/2 to 85/5. Stokes c Lyon b Starc 4(11) [4s-1]

Cummins to Root, out Lbw!! Appeaallll, Tucker says out LBW. How about height? The England captain doesn't bother reviewing too. This is class bowling from Cummins. So the first ball was full, then he pushed him back. Third was full and now he pushes him back again and gets it to nip back in sharply. Root was late on the defence, tried to adjust to the seam movement but the ball rushed him and hit the back leg in front of middle. Hit above the kneeroll, very interesting Root didn't bother about the review. Maybe because the back leg was bent a bit. Anyway, Cummins strikes for his team. Root lbw b Cummins 34(46) [4s-3]

Cummins to Malan, out Caught by Carey!! Oh England! Just as they desperately want to put on a show with the bat, they get out to soft dismissals. First the run-out of Burns, now a strangle down leg to a boundary ball. Full and down leg, Malan thought he had the glance to fine leg for four easy runs, but he hit it too soft and gets a tickle on it. Australia do hear this one. 78/3 as Carey takes a comfortable catch. In comes Ben Stokes! Malan c Carey b Cummins 25(64) [4s-5]

Cummins to Crawley, out Caught by Head!! And the line that should have been left alone outside off on a normal day by a batsman batting normally in a normal stance, ends up in being inside-edged from in front of the body to short leg. Cummins angles it in on a length, and Crawley defends with hard hands, onto his thigh pad, with Head taking a very sharp one over his head, and then juggling before holding on. Crawley c Head b Cummins 18(21) [4s-3]

Cummins to Crawley, out Rory Burns Run Out!! Absolute madness. As if getting undone by swing and seam wasn't enough already, England's opening troubles now have a run-out as well to boast about in their featherless cap. Crawley taps it into the covers and calls Burns through for a quick single. Alas, Burns is slow to respond, and Labuschagne nails a direct hit at the striker's end. Two inches short. Rory Burns run out (Labuschagne) 0(6)

Mark Wood to Starc, out Caught by Rory Burns!! Taken running back from square leg. Mark Wood with the short ball and Starc can't resist despite a trap set. It rushes onto him quicker and he hits the pull straight up in the air, slightly top-edgish and Burns runs back from square leg to take an easy catch. England strike early on day 2. Starc c Rory Burns b Mark Wood 3(17)

Mark Wood to Green, out Caught by Crawley!! The short ball has done it for Mark Wood. Green falls to the trap. Short ball and Green takes it on, pulls but doesn't time it too well, Crawley is in between deep square and deep mid-wicket and he completes the catch. For this ball, Wood again went round the wicket and got it outside off, end of a fine innings though from the talented Green. Wood finally can afford a smile. Green c Crawley b Mark Wood 74(109) [4s-8]

Woakes to Head, out Caught by Robinson!! "Noooo," he says and it's a dolly for mid-on. Travis Head very lucky that this didn't happen on 99. Almost an action replay of that mishit. Full delivery, he tried to wrist it over the infield over mid-wicket, but the ball hits the outside half and carries to mid-on this time. Head walks off disappointed but gets a great ovation. End of a brilliant innings. Head c Robinson b Woakes 101(113) [4s-12]

Broad to Labuschagne, out Bowled!! 134.1kph, unbelievable dismissal. "I have never ever seen that in Test cricket" says Michael Vaughan on air. Labuschagne is on all fours after his spikes slipped and the result is Broad hits the stumps. An exaggerated shuffle outside off even before the bowl came out of Broad's hand, but then the spikes slipped and Labuschagne fell. It was a full middle-stump ball and once the batter was on the ground, there was little chance of the bat making contact with the ball. A comical dismissal but England will take it. Broad is on a celebratory run. Bizarre dismissal and not surprisingly it is Labuschagne who is at the thick of it. A definite top 3 in the most weirdest dismissals ever list. Labuschagne b Broad 44(53) [4s-9]

Robinson to Smith, out Caught by Crawley!! Edgeddd and taken low at second slip. There is absolutely no chance you can escape this pitch and ball as a batter in these conditions. Just got to be lucky to survive. Back of a length pitching and nipping away sharply, Smith squared up in defence, thick edge the hands weren't soft enough on the handle for the ball to drop in front of the cordon. 12/3. Perfect chance for England to wrap this up quickly. Can Australia give a stunning reply? Smith c Crawley b Robinson 0(2)

Robinson to Smith, out Caught by Crawley!! Edgeddd and taken low at second slip. There is absolutely no chance you can escape this pitch and ball as a batter in these conditions. Just got to be lucky to survive. Back of a length pitching and nipping away sharply, Smith squared up in defence, thick edge the hands weren't soft enough on the handle for the ball to drop in front of the cordon. 12/3. Perfect chance for England to wrap this up quickly. Can Australia give a stunning reply? Smith c Crawley b Robinson 0(2)

Broad to Khawaja, out Caught by Root!! This edge goes straight to first slip and Crawley isn't coming across. Brilliant full outswinger, Khawaja doesn't resist the defence this time, he played thinking what if it cuts back in, but it moved away to find the edge. Khawaja drops his head and trudges off. England making proper use of green and overcast conditions. Khawaja c Root b Broad 6(26)

Robinson to Warner, out Caught by Crawley!! Edgeddd and taken well at second slip. That was flying off the edge, but Crawley was alert with bent knees. Got his hands up to the left to pouch with both hands. Lovely ball from Robinson. Fullish and nipping away, Warner had to play the line, pushed at with hard hands though and he had control over the shot. Out for a 22-ball duck. Big wicket for England very early. Over to Marnus for some proper cricket entertainment with the bat and a bit of commentary too. Warner c Crawley b Robinson 0(22)
